_comment: Run protocol values from Chapter 5 (evaluation.tex). 'decided': false marks values the chapter still lists as TODO/DECIDE; the runner and the metrics script use them as given here and copy them into every manifest.

prompts.corridor: Use the naoqi MCP server. You control a robot at the start of a corridor. Follow the corridor to its end, which is marked by a green panel, and stop in front of the panel. When the robot is there, call rest.
prompts.corridor_complex: Use the naoqi MCP server. You control a robot at the start of a corridor with several corners. Follow the corridor to its end, which is marked by a red wall, and stop in front of the wall. When the robot is there, call rest.
prompts.search: Use the naoqi MCP server. You control a robot in a room. Somewhere in the room in front of the robot, not behind it, there is a red ball. Find the ball and stop close to it, facing it. When the robot is there, call rest.

caps._source: Table 5.3 (tab:end_conditions): 2 x the task's longest successful pilot run and 2 x the most tool calls in a successful pilot run (author, 2026-10-19), from the pilots of 2026-10-15: Corridor 548.3 s / 36 calls, Complex corridor 1707.8 s / 72 calls, Search 441.1 s / 32 calls (recomputed from the pilot records with pilot/metrics.py, 2026-10-19); seconds rounded to the nearest

grace_period_s._source: Section 5.1.3 (Normal end): 30 s (author, 2026-10-15; every harness ended by itself within 17 s in the Corridor and Search pilots)

invalid_if._source: Section 5.1.3 (Invalid runs), decided by the author 2026-10-15: a provider error that remains after the harness's retries and reaching a subscription or account usage limit both make the run invalid (redone in place); any other failure at the task is a failure. pilot/metrics.py records the two as separate reasons.

min_real_time_factor._source: Section 5.1.1 (Simulated tasks): 0.9 (author, 2026-10-15); below it the run is invalid and repeated

search._source: Section 5.1.1 (Search, Success criteria), decided by the author 2026-10-15: the operator judges at the moment of rest whether the torso, projected on the floor, is within max_distance_m of the ball's surface; the ball need not be visible. A run starts only with the battery at 50 % or more; the robot may stay on its charger, and moving the charger cable is not an intervention.
search.distance: from the robot's torso, projected on the floor, to the ball's surface
search._decided_2026_10_15: author: the visibility condition is dropped; success is the operator's judgement that the torso, projected on the floor, is within max_distance_m of the ball's surface at rest (proximity only, as ObjectNav's oracle-visibility variant). Charging during runs is allowed (weak battery).
search._decided_2026_10_19: author, during the main runs (search-A5-20261019T100956Z kicked the ball about 1 m while walking past it): a ball the robot moves is judged where it lies at rest, like any other run; the operator notes the move in the verdict. A clarification of the criterion as written, not a change.
